sources.title: OWASP MASVS
sources.use: The 24 MASVS v2 controls each finding maps to (taxonomy/masvs.json), and the eight control groups findings are reported under.

sources.title: OWASP MASTG
sources.use: The iOS tests, techniques and best practices behind each check (taxonomy/mastg.json, synced from upstream).

sources.title: OWASP MASWE
sources.use: Weakness catalogue with its MASVS control, CWE and profile mappings (taxonomy/maswe.json); the second level of the cluster rollup.

sources.title: Apple Developer Documentation
sources.use: The normative definition of every Info.plist key, entitlement, framework and API symbol a rule keys on.

sources.title: Apple Platform Security Guide
sources.use: Data-protection classes, keychain accessibility semantics, Secure Enclave, Lockdown Mode.

sources.title: FIRST CVSS v4.0
sources.use: Qualitative severity bands anchoring every derived security severity.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK for Mobile
sources.terms: ATT&CK Terms of Use (free use, attribution)
sources.use: Technique IDs (T1xxx) tagged on vectors and findings.

sources.title: MITRE CWE
sources.use: CWE ids as MASWE maps them to each weakness, for readers who work in CWE.

sources.title: NIST (CSRC publications and NVD)
sources.use: Cryptographic primitive status: which algorithms are deprecated, disallowed, or approved.

sources.title: IETF RFCs
sources.use: Protocol-level definitions: TLS versions, JWT, URI schemes, Bonjour/DNS-SD.

sources.title: Citizen Lab
sources.use: Mercenary-spyware indicators: Pegasus, Predator, QuaDream, Candiru, Paragon.

sources.title: Kaspersky Securelist
sources.use: Operation Triangulation / TriangleDB indicators.

sources.title: Coalition Against Stalkerware / EFF
sources.use: Consumer-stalkerware family and capability definitions.

sources.title: US Federal Trade Commission
sources.use: Named location and data brokers (TRK-02), and tracker attribution grounded in enforcement actions.

sources.title: LINDDUN privacy threat taxonomy
sources.use: Privacy threat categories bound per construct in the crosswalk.

sources.title: EUR-Lex (GDPR and EU regulation)
sources.use: GDPR articles cited on transparency, consent and data-residency findings.

sources.title: Exodus Privacy
sources.use: Independent tracker-prevalence benchmark cited in dashboard context.

sources.title: First-party SDK vendor documentation
sources.use: The vendor's own description of an SDK this scanner fingerprints: the authoritative statement of what that SDK is and what it collects. Used only to identify an SDK, never as a security claim.

sources.title: Mozilla Public Suffix List
sources.use: Registrable domains of every endpoint, private section included, so tenants of shared hosting (appspot.com, blob.core.windows.net) are not merged into one owner. Vendored at Rules/domains/public_suffix_list.dat.

sources.title: IAB Europe Transparency & Consent Framework
sources.use: The Global Vendor List format, used to recognise a bundled vendor list so its hundreds of vendor privacy-policy URLs are not read as endpoints the app contacts.
